stages.title: Foundations
stages.summary: What a computer actually is and does, and how to talk to it.

topics.title: How computers work
topics.summary: CPU, memory, storage, and programs as lists of instructions.
topics.why: Every line of code you write becomes instructions for this machine. Knowing its parts makes error messages, speed and memory make sense.

resources.title: Khan Academy: Computers and the Internet
Harvard CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science

topics.title: Binary and data
topics.summary: How everything (numbers, text, images) is stored as 0s and 1s.
topics.why: Binary explains why 0.1 + 0.2 isn't exactly 0.3, what a 'byte' is, and how text becomes numbers. It's the alphabet of computing.

topics.title: Memory
topics.summary: RAM as numbered boxes, and how Python names point to values.
topics.why: Many confusing bugs, like 'I changed one list and the other changed too', come from how values live in memory.

resources.title: Facts and myths about Python names and values (Ned Batchelder)
Python Tutor: watch your code run, step by step

topics.title: The terminal
topics.summary: Typing commands to your computer instead of clicking.
topics.why: Developers run programs, install tools and use Git from the terminal every day. It's the professional's remote control.

resources.title: Ubuntu: The command line for beginners

topics.title: Files and folders
topics.summary: The file system tree, paths, and file extensions.
topics.why: Programs read and write files all the time. Understanding paths fixes the classic 'FileNotFoundError'.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff: Reading and Writing Files
Ubuntu: The command line for beginners

stages.title: Programming basics
stages.summary: The building blocks found in every programming language.

topics.title: Variables
topics.summary: Giving names to values so you can use them later.
topics.why: Variables are how a program remembers things. Nearly every line of code reads or changes one.

resources.title: Harvard CS50P: Introduction to Programming with Python

topics.title: Data types
topics.summary: Numbers, text, True/False and None, and converting between them.
topics.why: The type of a value decides what you can do with it. Type mix-ups are one of the most common beginner errors.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff: Python Basics

topics.title: Conditionals (if / else)
topics.summary: Letting your program make decisions.
topics.why: Without decisions a program does the same thing every time. Conditionals make it react to input.

resources.title: Python Tutorial: More Control Flow Tools
Automate the Boring Stuff: Flow Control

topics.title: Loops
topics.summary: Repeating work with for and while.
topics.why: Computers shine at repetition. Loops let ten lines of code process a million items.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff: Flow Control (loops)
Python Tutorial: for statements and range()

topics.title: Functions
topics.summary: Packaging code into reusable, named pieces.
topics.why: Functions are how real programs stay organized. They let you name an idea, reuse it, and test it on its own.

topics.title: Data structures
topics.summary: Lists, tuples, dictionaries and sets: holding many values.
topics.why: Real data comes in collections: a list of users, a dictionary of prices. Picking the right structure makes code simpler and faster.

stages.title: Python in depth
stages.summary: The tools for writing real, organized Python programs.

topics.title: Object-oriented programming
topics.summary: Classes and objects: bundling data with the code that uses it.
topics.why: Most large codebases and libraries are built from classes. You'll read and write them constantly.

resources.title: Real Python: Object-Oriented Programming in Python

topics.title: Modules and imports
topics.summary: Splitting code into files and using other people's code.
topics.why: No one writes everything from scratch. Imports let you use Python's huge standard library and your own files.

resources.title: Python Tutorial: Brief Tour of the Standard Library

topics.title: Errors and exceptions
topics.summary: Reading tracebacks and handling problems gracefully.
topics.why: Errors are not failures, they're information. Reading them well is the fastest way to get unstuck.

topics.title: Working with files
topics.summary: Reading and writing text files from Python.
topics.why: Saving results, reading data, processing logs: files are how programs remember things after they stop.

resources.title: Python Tutorial: Reading and Writing Files
Automate the Boring Stuff: Reading and Writing Files

topics.title: Working with APIs
topics.summary: Asking other programs and websites for data.
topics.why: Weather, maps, payments, AI: modern apps are built by connecting to APIs. It's how your code talks to the world.

resources.title: Real Python: Python and REST APIs
Public APIs: a big list of free APIs to practice with

stages.title: Tools
stages.summary: The everyday toolkit of a working developer.

topics.title: The command line, deeper
topics.summary: Moving files, searching, pipes, and the PATH.
topics.why: Once you're comfortable here, you can automate boring work and fix setup problems that confuse most beginners.

resources.title: MIT Missing Semester: Shell Tools and Scripting

topics.title: VS Code
topics.summary: Getting the most out of your code editor.
topics.why: You'll spend thousands of hours in your editor. A few shortcuts and features save hours every week.

topics.title: Git
topics.summary: Saving the history of your code with commits and branches.
topics.why: Every software team uses Git. It's your undo button, your diary and your teamwork tool in one.

topics.title: GitHub
topics.summary: Sharing code online, collaborating, and showing your work.
topics.why: GitHub is where open source lives and where employers look at your projects. Your profile is part of your resume.

topics.title: Virtual environments
topics.summary: Giving each Python project its own set of libraries.
topics.why: Without them, projects fight over library versions. With them, any project can be set up again with one command.

resources.title: Python Tutorial: Virtual Environments and Packages

topics.title: Debugging
topics.summary: A calm, step-by-step way to find and fix bugs.
topics.why: Developers spend more time fixing code than writing it. Debugging is a skill you can learn, not a talent.

resources.title: MIT Missing Semester: Debugging and Profiling
Python docs: pdb, the Python debugger

stages.title: How the web works
stages.summary: What really happens between your browser and a website.

topics.title: HTTP
topics.summary: The request-and-response language of the web.
topics.why: Every web page, API call and form submission is an HTTP request. It's the language backends and frontends share.

topics.title: DNS
topics.summary: How a name like example.com becomes a computer's address.
topics.why: When a site 'can't be found', DNS is often why. It's also a step in deploying anything with its own domain name.

topics.title: Browsers
topics.summary: How a browser turns HTML, CSS and JavaScript into a page.
topics.why: Knowing what the browser does helps you build pages that load fast and debug them with developer tools.

topics.title: Servers
topics.summary: The computers that answer requests.
topics.why: Backend development means writing the code that runs on servers. This is the other half of every web app.

resources.title: MDN: What is a web server?

topics.title: HTML and CSS
topics.summary: The structure (HTML) and style (CSS) of web pages.
topics.why: Every website is built from these two. Even backend developers need to read and tweak them.

topics.title: JavaScript basics
topics.summary: The programming language of the browser.
topics.why: JavaScript makes pages interactive, and it's the most used language in the world. Your Python skills transfer directly.

stages.title: Data
stages.summary: Storing, organizing and asking questions of data.

topics.title: JSON
topics.summary: The most common text format for sending data.
topics.why: APIs, config files and DevPath's own content all use JSON. You'll read it every day.

topics.title: Databases
topics.summary: Programs that store data safely and let you search it fast.
topics.why: Almost every real app keeps its data in a database. DevPath will too, one day.

topics.title: SQL
topics.summary: The language for asking databases questions.
topics.why: SQL is 50 years old and still everywhere. It's one of the most valuable skills on any developer job listing.

stages.title: Computer science
stages.summary: Ways of thinking about problems and the speed of solutions.

topics.title: Algorithms
topics.summary: Step-by-step recipes for solving problems.
topics.why: Thinking in algorithms helps you break any problem into steps, and it's what coding interviews test.

topics.title: Big-O notation
topics.summary: Describing how code slows down as data grows.
topics.why: Big-O tells you whether code that works on 10 items will still work on 10 million. Interviewers ask about it a lot.

resources.title: Python Wiki: Time complexity of built-in operations

topics.title: Recursion
topics.summary: Functions that call themselves on smaller problems.
topics.why: Recursion is the natural way to handle trees, like folders inside folders, and it powers fast sorting algorithms.

resources.title: Python Tutor: watch the call stack grow

topics.title: Searching
topics.summary: Linear search vs. binary search.
topics.why: Binary search turns a million steps into about 20. It's the classic example of a clever algorithm paying off.

topics.title: Sorting
topics.summary: Putting things in order, slowly and quickly.
topics.why: Sorting algorithms are the best playground for comparing approaches and understanding Big-O.

stages.title: Engineering practice
stages.summary: The habits that turn code into software other people can trust.

topics.title: Clean code
topics.summary: Writing code that other humans can read.
topics.why: Code is read far more often than it's written, including by future you. Clean code is a kindness and a career skill.

resources.title: PEP 8: Style Guide for Python Code

topics.title: Testing
topics.summary: Code that checks your code.
topics.why: Tests let you change code without fear. Teams expect them, and writing them makes you think about edge cases.

resources.title: Real Python: Getting Started With Testing in Python

topics.title: Code review
topics.summary: Reading each other's code before it's merged.
topics.why: On a team, every change gets reviewed. Giving and receiving feedback well is how developers grow fastest.

resources.title: GitHub Docs: About pull request reviews

topics.title: Documentation
topics.summary: READMEs, comments and docstrings that help people.
topics.why: A project without docs is a project nobody can use, including you in six months.

stages.title: Building real software
stages.summary: Putting everything together into apps people can use.

topics.title: Backend with FastAPI
topics.summary: Building your own web API in Python.
topics.why: This is where your Python, HTTP and JSON skills combine into something real: a server other apps can talk to.

topics.title: A simple frontend
topics.summary: A web page that talks to your API.
topics.why: A backend is invisible without a frontend. Connecting the two makes you a 'full-stack' developer.

topics.title: Deployment
topics.summary: Putting your app on the internet for anyone to use.
topics.why: A deployed project with a real link is worth ten that only run on your laptop, especially to employers.

stages.title: Career
stages.summary: Showing your skills and landing your first developer job.

topics.title: Portfolio
topics.summary: A small collection of projects that shows what you can do.
topics.why: Without professional experience yet, your projects ARE your experience. A good portfolio gets you interviews.

resources.title: GitHub Docs: Managing your profile README

topics.title: Resume
topics.summary: A one-page summary that gets you past the first filter.
topics.why: Recruiters spend seconds on each resume. A clear one with real projects stands out.

topics.title: Interviews
topics.summary: Coding challenges, technical questions and behavioral questions.
topics.why: Interviewing is its own skill, and practice is what makes the difference. You can get good at it.

resources.title: NeetCode: practice problems with video explanations
